outcome.decision: Raised the federal funds target range 25bp to 3.75–4.00%, unanimous 12-0 vote — the Fed's first rate hike in three years. New SEP median points to 4.1% at end of 2026 and 2027, with the longer-run rate at 3.2%.
outcome.reaction: Widely anticipated (markets had ~83–85% odds of the hike priced going in); the unanimity was the surprise. Markets repriced toward one more 25bp hike in December.

events.detail: September inflation (BLS, 8:30 AM ET). First CPI read after the Sep FOMC; sets the tone for Oct 28.
events.label: CPI Sep 2026

outcome.decision: September CPI printed hot (BLS, Oct 14, 8:30 AM ET): headline +0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y; core +0.3% m/m, 2.6% y/y — core a tenth above the +0.2% consensus anchor, with gasoline (+9.1% m/m) driving over half the headline increase.
outcome.reaction: The 10-year spiked ~9bp intraday to ~5.31% but closed Oct 14 at 5.19% — inside the 5.2–5.5% containment band, not a falsifier trip. October hike odds repriced from ~22% to roughly 40% for the Oct 27–28 FOMC. Bank credit did not crack on the print (BAC's drop was a $1.2B Treasury settlement charge, not provisions).

events.watch_out_for: Whether shelter disinflation resumes; the spread between the consensus print and the whisper numbers matters more than the headline.

events.detail: Oct 27-28 meeting, six days before the midterms.
events.label: FOMC Decision Oct 27-28

outcome.decision: Held the federal funds target range at 3.75–4.00% on a 10-2 vote — Hammack and Cook dissented in favor of a 25bp hike. Statement: inflation remains elevated relative to 2%; activity expanding at a solid pace. IORB unchanged at 3.90%.
outcome.reaction: Muted: S&P 500 +0.28% to 7,743.98, VIX 16.91, 10Y 5.05%. Two hawkish dissents kept December live — CME FedWatch priced ~83% odds of a 25bp December hike after the decision. Minutes due Nov 18.

events.watch_out_for: Whether Warsh signals a second consecutive hike — markets priced roughly 60% odds of +25bp in late September; a hold would need soft CPI and jobs prints first.

events.detail: Since 1962 the S&P 500 has never been negative in the 12 months after midterms (avg +12-16%).
events.label: US Midterm Elections

outcome.decision: Democrats won control of both chambers (AP calls): the Senate flipped from a 53-47 Republican majority, and the House flipped with Hakeem Jeffries in line for Speaker. Result is divided government for the last two years of the Trump term; no veto-proof majority.
outcome.reaction: Clean, uncontested outcome — the post-midterm base rate (gridlock continuity) applies. S&P 500 +1.58% on Nov 4 to 7,688.62 and VIX fell 20.83 → 16.61; the relief did not hold — the index dropped 4.36% the next day on the AI-capex selloff, unrelated to the vote.

events.watch_out_for: Clean vs contested outcome for House/Senate control — the post-midterm stat assumes the gridlock-continuity read, not a disputed count.

events.detail: October payrolls. Labor-market read heading into the Dec FOMC.
events.label: NFP Oct 2026

outcome.decision: October payrolls +165K vs ~65K consensus; unemployment 4.1% (vs 4.2% expected); average hourly earnings +0.4% m/m, +3.1% y/y; participation 61.9%. August–September revised up a combined 84K. Soft spots: U-6 rose to 7.9% from 7.6%; part-time jobs +339K.
outcome.reaction: Hawkish: 10Y +3bp to ~4.87%, 2Y +6bp to ~4.53%, dollar index +0.7%; December hike odds rose to ~78% from 70% (LSEG). Equities bounced anyway after Thursday's rout — S&P 500 +0.31% to 7,376.86, Nasdaq +1.1% — but the S&P lost 2.7% on the week.

events.watch_out_for: Whether job gains keep pace with workforce growth and unemployment holds steady — cooling without cracking keeps the December-hike debate alive.

events.detail: October inflation (BLS, 8:30 AM ET). First CPI after the October hold; with payrolls hot, a firm core print cements a December hike.
events.label: CPI Oct 2026

outcome.decision: October CPI +0.4% m/m vs +0.3% consensus (September +0.6%); core +0.3% m/m vs +0.2% consensus (second straight 0.3%). No 12-month rate published — BLS has no October 2025 baseline after the 2025 shutdown. Shelter +0.3% (>30% of the headline gain); energy +0.7% (gasoline +1.0%, electricity +0.9%); food +0.5%; transportation services +0.8%; used cars -1.2%.
outcome.reaction: Hawkish: CME FedWatch fully priced a 25bp December hike and 50bp odds rose to ~14% from ~0. S&P 500 -0.38% to 7,520.93 (off an intraday low near -0.7%); VIX 19.92 to 19.46; MOVE 85.98 to 92.43; DXY +0.6% to 102.23. Equities recovered next session: S&P +1.31% to 7,619.38 on Nov 11, VIX 17.49.

events.watch_out_for: Core m/m vs +0.3%: a second straight hot core print removes the last argument for a December pause; gasoline reversal could flatter the headline.

events.detail: Nvidia reports after the close (call 2 PM PT). Guide was $108.0B ±2% revenue, 74.0% ±0.5pt gross margin; consensus ~$108.8B / $2.47 EPS.
events.label: NVDA Q3 FY27 earnings
events.watch_out_for: Data-center guide and hyperscaler capex commentary — the read-through for SMH, VRT, VST and the AI-capex correction episode.

events.detail: Minutes of the October hold (2 PM ET).
events.label: FOMC Minutes (Oct 27-28)
events.watch_out_for: How many participants beyond the two dissenters leaned toward a hike, and any balance-sheet discussion.

events.detail: Personal Income and Outlays, October (BEA, 8:30 AM ET). September PCE spending rose 0.5%, saving rate 3.8%.
events.label: PCE Oct 2026
events.watch_out_for: Core PCE m/m — the Fed's preferred gauge two weeks before the December decision.

events.detail: Dec 8-9 meeting, year-end, new SEP. October held 10-2 with two hike dissents, so this is the next hike window — markets price ~78–83% odds of +25bp after the hot October jobs report.
events.label: FOMC Decision Dec 8-9
events.watch_out_for: Hike vs hold, how many dissents, and the 2027 dot median — which sets the rate path into next year. Oct CPI (Nov 10) and Oct PCE (Nov 25) are the last inflation reads before it.

events.detail: November inflation (BLS, 8:30 AM ET), the day after the December FOMC decision.
events.label: CPI Nov 2026
events.watch_out_for: Whether the December decision is validated or second-guessed by the print.
